consequential_claim_checks.independent_assessment: route_id/trip_id/service_id and stop IDs are distinct; service_id dates are calendar rules plus exceptions. Calendar-only or dates-only forms exist.
consequential_claim_checks.conditions_types_units_domain_exceptions: IDs are CSV strings/foreign references; service dates use YYYYMMDD; not realtime instance IDs.

consequential_claim_checks.independent_assessment: Agency timezone governs stop_times; service day can extend beyond 24 hours; DST basis differs from naive midnight arithmetic.
consequential_claim_checks.conditions_types_units_domain_exceptions: GTFS HH:MM:SS Time is not POSIX time. Stop timezone is not the timetable timezone.

consequential_claim_checks.judgment: SUPPORTED IN FINAL; PREDECESSOR GAP CORRECTED
consequential_claim_checks.independent_assessment: exact_times=0/empty is headway service; 1 is schedule-based compression. Exact_times=0 does not authorize invented exact static departures.
consequential_claim_checks.conditions_types_units_domain_exceptions: headway_secs is a positive integer in seconds; exact_times optional default 0/empty.

consequential_claim_checks.independent_assessment: Ordinary static trips may use trip_id; frequency instances need date/time; long/late collisions require date; alternate nonfrequency key must be unique. NEW is explicitly outside an existing-static-trip lookup.
consequential_claim_checks.conditions_types_units_domain_exceptions: NEW requires novel trip_id plus existing route_id; zero static match is expected for that relationship, not invalid. F-01.

consequential_claim_checks.independent_assessment: Realtime protocol version and static revision are different. RT feed_version is optional and matches static publisher text. Missing version is not verified alignment.
consequential_claim_checks.conditions_types_units_domain_exceptions: Static feed_version Text is recommended; RT field string optional. Fail-closed display is a local proposal, not a mandatory consumer behavior.

consequential_claim_checks.conditions_types_units_domain_exceptions: StopTimeEvent.time is int64 POSIX seconds; delay is int32 signed seconds; NO_DATA forbids prediction time/delay, while NEW/REPLACEMENT can still carry scheduled_time.

consequential_claim_checks.independent_assessment: UNSCHEDULED only exact_times=0; NEW supplies a complete journey; REPLACEMENT identifies original but supplies alternate stop/times; DUPLICATED references source through TripDescriptor and new identity through TripProperties; DELETED differs from CANCELED.

material_findings.classification: material wrong / unsupported consequential acceptance rule
material_findings.title: Universal static-trip matching gate conflicts with conditionally supported NEW trips

candidate_locators.text: Resolve each TripUpdate to exactly one trip instance in the exact approved schedule:

- The specification permits a fallback combination of `route_id`, `direction_id`, `start_time` and `start_date` only if it resolves uniquely. If a descriptor resolves to zero or multiple instances, reject or quarantine that entity and report realtime unavailable for it. [S02, S03]
- `NEW`: an unrelated added trip with its full stop/time journey specified.

Use only message types the regional partner confirms it actually supplies. For a scheduled trip, accept a TripUpdate only when it matches the exact trip instance and an approved schedule version. Display the published schedule time and, where a valid fresh producer time exists, a clearly separate “Realtime update” time/status. GTFS-RT event times can be producer estimates; without partner semantics do not label one an observed vessel position or a guaranteed ETA. [S02, S03]

governing_primary_locators.condition: TripDescriptor distinguishes NEW from identifying an existing GTFS trip. NEW trip_id must be absent from static GTFS; route_id must exist in routes.txt.
The trip_id field has relationship-specific identity rules; NEW is not an existing-static-trip lookup.
NEW supplies its complete journey through StopTimeUpdates; REPLACEMENT also supplies its own journey.

material_findings.analysis: The final directs every TripUpdate to resolve to one instance in the exact approved schedule and directs zero-match descriptors to be rejected/quarantined. It later explicitly includes NEW in the conditional support inventory and describes the full journey correctly, but never makes NEW an exception to the prior static-trip acceptance gate. A valid NEW trip necessarily has no static trip_id match. Thus the stated gate would hide an otherwise valid partner-supported extra ferry service. This is a conflict in the proposal, not a claim that the unknown ferry partner supplies NEW.

analytical_counterexample.status: PROSPECTIVE SEMANTIC COUNTEREXAMPLE; NOT AN EXECUTED PRODUCT TEST
analytical_counterexample.inputs: An approved static dataset with route R and two known terminal stop IDs, plus a fresh version-bound NEW TripUpdate whose novel trip_id N is not in trips.txt and whose complete StopTimeUpdates specify the journey.
analytical_counterexample.source_permitted_behavior: NEW identifies a new trip using N and existing route/stop references; absence of N in trips.txt is required rather than invalid.
analytical_counterexample.proposal_gate_behavior: N produces zero existing-static-trip matches and is quarantined by the universal gate.
analytical_counterexample.material_effect: Declared extra service can disappear from the public board even when its source binding, freshness, route, stops and relationship support are valid.

material_findings.counterevidence_considered: The final correctly says NEW is unrelated to an existing trip and supplies a full journey; it also says REPLACEMENT does not use the original static schedule. Those are credited. They do not state which acceptance gate bypasses the explicit each-TripUpdate/static-schedule/zero-match rejection rule. Reading the latter as ordinary scheduled trips only would import an exception the final no longer states.
material_findings.lineage: The draft explicitly limited this acceptance statement to a scheduled trip. The final broadens it to each TripUpdate while expanding the relationship inventory. C-04 correctly requested relationship-specific semantics, but its final treatment leaves this consequential acceptance conflict.
material_findings.not_required: This finding does not require NEW support when the partner does not supply it, a prototype, an implementation, or a deployment. It evaluates the proposal on its own declared conditional support.
